Title: Admins' mail-enabled security groups created through the admin center UI may be provisioned incorrectly

User impact: Admins' mail-enabled security groups created through the admin center UI may be provisioned incorrectly.

More info: Specifically, when admins attempt to create mail-enabled security groups in the Exchange admin center, they may be provisioned as a regular distribution group rather than a mail-enabled security group.

Current status: We're investigating a potential issue with Exchange Online and checking for impact to your organization. We'll provide an update within 30 minutes.

Title: Admins' mail-enabled security groups created through the admin center UI may be provisioned incorrectly

User impact: Admins' mail-enabled security groups created through the admin center UI may be provisioned incorrectly.

More info: Specifically, when admins attempt to create mail-enabled security groups in the Exchange admin center, they may be provisioned as a regular distribution group rather than a mail-enabled security group.

Current status: We're reviewing service logs and contextual details provided by a subset of affected users to gain insight into the underlying source of impact and determine our next steps.

Scope of impact: Any admins attempting to create mail-enabled security groups in the Exchange admin center are affected. This section may be updated as our investigation continues.

Next update by: Wednesday, November 18, 2026, at 9:30 AM UTC

Title: Admins' mail-enabled security groups created through the admin center UI may be provisioned incorrectly

User impact: Admins' mail-enabled security groups created through the admin center UI may be provisioned incorrectly.

More info: Specifically, when admins attempt to create mail-enabled security groups in the Exchange admin center (EAC) or Microsoft 365 admin center (MAC), the groups may be provisioned as regular distribution groups rather than mail-enabled security groups. As a workaround, admins may be able to use PowerShell to create mail-enabled security groups.

Current status: We're continuing to review service logs and contextual details, including HTTP Archive (HAR) logs provided by a subset of affected users, to identify the root cause of the issue and determine an appropriate mitigation plan.

Scope of impact: Some admins located in Japan that are attempting to create mail-enabled security groups in the Exchange admin center or Microsoft 365 admin center may be affected. This section may be updated as our investigation continues.

Next update by: Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 7:00 PM UTC

Title: Admins' mail-enabled security groups created through the admin center UI may be provisioned incorrectly

User impact: Admins' mail-enabled security groups created through the admin center UI may be provisioned incorrectly.

Current status: We've updated the "Title", "User impact", "More info", and "Scope of impact" sections to more accurately convey our current understanding of the impact. We've identified a recent service change designed to adjust the way our service handles requests to create security and distribution groups that's missing a necessary configuration and is causing impact. We're testing the reversal of this change to ensure that it remediates the impact as expected.

Scope of impact: Some admins attempting to create mail-enabled security groups in the Exchange admin center or Microsoft 365 admin center may be affected. This section may be updated as our investigation continues.

Title: Admins' mail-enabled security groups created through the admin center UI may be provisioned incorrectly

User impact: Admins' mail-enabled security groups created through the admin center UI may be provisioned incorrectly.

Impact is specific to mail-enabled security groups that are created with only one owner and one member.

Current status: We're continuing to reverse the impacting service change to remediate the impact. 

Scope of impact: Some admins attempting to create mail-enabled security groups in the Exchange admin center or Microsoft 365 admin center may be affected. This section may be updated as our investigation continues.

Title: Admins' mail-enabled security groups created through the admin center UI may be provisioned incorrectly

User impact: Admins' mail-enabled security groups created through the admin center UI may have been provisioned incorrectly.

More info: Specifically, when admins attempted to create mail-enabled security groups in the Exchange admin center (EAC) or Microsoft 365 admin center, the groups may have been provisioned as regular distribution groups rather than mail-enabled security groups. As a workaround, admins may have been able to use PowerShell to create mail-enabled security groups.

Impact was specific to mail-enabled security groups that are created with only one owner and one member.

Final status: We've completed deployment of our fix and confirmed through internal testing that the impact is remediated. All newly created mail-enabled security groups created through the Exchange admin center or Microsoft 365 admin center will be created as designed. Affected admins will need to recreate any groups provisioned incorrectly during the duration of the impact.

Scope of impact: Some admins that attempted to create mail-enabled security groups in the Exchange admin center or Microsoft 365 admin center may have been affected.

Start time: Tuesday, October 13, 2026, at 9:34 AM UTC

End time: Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 10:47 PM UTC

Root cause: A recent service change designed to adjust the way our service handles requests to create security and distribution groups was missing a necessary configuration and resulted in impact.

Next steps: 
- We're reviewing our service change testing and validation procedures to identify and prevent similar issues with missing configurations impacting security and distribution group creation requests from occurring in the future.

This is the final update for this event.
